title: A Rattlesnake Shakes Its Tail 90 Times a Second

scenes.text: A rattlesnake shakes its tail ninety times every second.
That is about twice as fast as the wing muscles of a hummingbird.
The rattle is made of dead tissue, like your fingernails.
Special muscles in the tail do the work, and they can keep going for minutes, sometimes hours.
They are the fastest muscles of any vertebrate.
A warning you can hear before you see.

description:
A rattlesnake's tail muscles contract up to ninety times per second, faster than a hummingbird's wing muscles.
The rattle itself is dead tissue, and the muscles can keep going for minutes at a time.
Have you ever heard one in person?
first_comment: Each new segment is added when the snake sheds its skin. Would you recognise the sound?
